text:
Raj: heads-up — CI perf alert on release/1.12 rolling. 99th token latency jumped ~2.8x after last merge window, perf-suite failing on staging :eyes:
ci-bot: perf-suite/staging failed: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/9876 (regression detected, baseline vs HEAD)
Michelle: saw that. top suspect is PR #4821 (batching rewrite). it switched selector to prefer `max_batch_size` which can force bigger batches and increase queuing tail under skewed seqlen
Danny: also interesting: PR #4815 tweaked KV cache sampling rate (lowered hot-sample retention). might increase KV cache misses and force more kv lookup latency in hot paths
Olga: can we bisect between the two PRs? unclear which one amplified tail. propose: bisect on merging order using the release branch and run perf-suite headless.
Raj: agreed. order of operations: 1) reproduce locally, 2) narrow to PR, 3) if PR is root cause, either revert or feature-flag backport to release branch.
Michelle: repro command I used locally (small cluster):
```
./scripts/perf_run.sh --model=gpt-medium --workload=chatty --profile=tail latency --iters=500 --seed=42
```
results: flamegraph shows hot in `batch_selector::score_batch()` ~34% and `kv_cache::evict_if_needed()` ~18%
ci-bot: profiling artifact: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/9876/flamegraph.svg
Danny: I ran the bisect draft: cherry-pick PR #4815 onto release only -> perf metric stable; cherry-pick #4821 onto release -> reproduces spike. so #4821 is primary suspect.
Olga: nice. what's inside #4821 exactly? any easy toggle?
Michelle: yes — there's a flag `feature.batch_selector_strict=true` in runtime flags. original plan was to flip on later. we enabled by default in that PR.
Raj: if toggling the flag fixes it, we can do hotfix: 1) revert merge of #4821 on main (fast), 2) cherry-pick a small PR to release/1.12 that sets the flag false and run canary. prefer cherry-pick so main history stays intact until we engineer a nicer solution.
Danny: I'll open a small hotpatch: PR 4830 -> `release/1.12` set `feature.batch_selector_strict=false` and include test that asserts average batch size distribution unchanged. linking in a sec.
Danny: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4830 : backport toggle + release notes: "temporary disable strict batch selector to mitigate tail latency regression" :shipit:
release-lead: pls coordinate with QA/Canary. we need perf-suite pass on staging + 48h canary on a small percentage of traffic before full rollout. also notify customers on Dedicated if SLA-sensitive.
Olga: I'll run staging canary now with PR 4830 cherry-picked. running perf-suite and tail monitors.
ci-bot: staging perf run queued: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/9881 (triggered by PR 4830)
Olga: quick snapshot from profiler after toggle: `batch_selector::score_batch()` down to ~9%, `kv_cache::evict_if_needed()` unchanged at ~17%. 99th latency back to baseline +/-5%
Raj: good. once CI green, merge cherry-pick to release, then follow with main revert plan if we want to revert the default on main too.
Michelle: action items: Danny -> push PR 4830 (done). Olga -> confirm staging perf green (in progress). Raj -> draft revert plan for main if needed. Danny -> add followup ticket to rework selector (reduce strictness but keep correctness).
Olga: staging perf-suite PASS. canary started (5% traffic). monitoring dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/latency/rel-1-12-canary
Raj: thumbs — keep an eye for 2 hours, if no regressions we'll widen. thanks all :thumbsup:
ci-bot: perf-suite/staging passed at 2012345845
Olga: widening canary to 25% now. no anomalies in last 30m.
release-lead: noted. will schedule a quick postmortem doc for incident timeline and next steps on selector rework. assign owners and ETA 2 weeks.
Michelle: adding a guard in code to avoid large queued batches when seqlen-skew detected, that should be lower-risk than full strict mode. filing PR draft today.
Raj: great. closing loop once main revert decision made. thanks everyone.
